subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.
reasoning:
I'm planning an alebrije combining jaguar body and eagle head, with folded wings and feathered tail, designed at a manageable scale and complexity while keeping the SDK structure correct.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton: spine chain from hips through chest, a neck chain leading to the head and jaw joints, a tail chain extending backward with multiple segments, and front/back leg chains using two-bone limbs with named shoulder, elbow, and paw joints.

I'm setting up the hind legs as three-segment digitigrade limbs (hip, knee, hock, paw), parented to the hips, while front legs stay two-segment and parent to the chest joint. Paw contact points sit near floor level, each represented with a flattened box or sphere shape.

For the body, I'm sweeping a tapered tube along the spine-to-chest path for the torso, then adding small cone or sphere toes and talon-like claws for the front feet. I'll keep the painted details flat-color for now—cream belly, orange back, and scattered rosette-style spots in alternating magenta, teal, and ink tones—saving texture work for a later stage.

Now I'm shaping the eagle head: a skull sphere at the head joint with a curved cone-swept upper beak and a separate lower beak hinged at a jaw joint, plus yellow eyes with black pupils and brow ridges, all oriented using local forward/up/left directions relative to the head.

For the neck, I'm adding a ruff of flattened spikes arranged in a ring, alternating colors around each item, and then planning a row of crest spikes along the top of the head using local head-space points.

Now I'm adding round jaguar-style ears on top of the head with pink inner spheres, plus deciding wing placement from the shoulders in an extended rest pose.

I'm building each wing as a bone chain from shoulder through elbow to wrist/tip, parented to spine2, then attaching flattened feather shapes along the chain using repeated swept blade sections.

Writing feather extrusion code...

Still writing the wing feather sweep code...

Still working out feather orientation...

Defining feather tip geometry...

Adding leg stripe bands and sock colors, then scattering hit-spot decals across the body surface with layered ink discs beneath for depth.

Skipping extra wing dots and chest scale plates for now, leaving those plain for a later stage. I'm verifying paw and leg bottoms rest flush with the floor, and positioning the yellow sphere eyes relative to the head's local coordinate space.

Now placing black pupils offset further out and forward on the eyes, adding an angled brow rod over each eye, and sizing the head sphere with a slight scale distortion for an eagle-like shape.

For stage two I'll add the cere nub above the beak and build the neck as a chain of two joints running from the spine tip up to the head, with the head joint parented at the end of the neck and tapering tube radii along its length.

Now I'm working out the beak as a small forward extension from the head sphere, then shaping the spine chain itself—placing hips, spine1, and spine2 joints so the body sweep runs from hips to chest with a rounded rump cap behind.

With leg and neck anchor points settled, I'm now sketching color sectors for the body (belly cream patch, back orange stripe) and picking a warm orange base tone, laying out the full palette of orange, yellow, magenta, teal, blue, green, red, ink, and cream to use across the design.

Now I'm defining the tail as a curved chain of points extending back and up from the hips, tapering its width toward the tip, and alternating colored bands along its length using a cyclic color function, finishing with a feather fan at the tail's end.

Setting up wing bones with a chain of shoulder, elbow, and wrist points scaled outward, so feathers along the wing can attach to each joint.

Still adjusting feather angles...

I'm layering in coverts and marginal feathers with alternating primary colors, then planning a checklist of remaining detail work: eyes, beak patterns, chest scales, jaguar-like rosettes on the flank, wing covert patterns, ruff barbs, and paw claws with toe detailing.

Now I'm positioning each decorative piece with specific coordinates and normals—face mask, beak decor, chest plumage, flank rosettes, wing dots, and front talons—working through the body's half-width constraints to place them correctly on the sides, then moving on to hind talons and tail ring texture as part of the overall body pattern.

Naming each part uniquely for mirroring (body, wingArmL, feather segments) and setting up texture requests for rosettes, stripes, tail tube, and neck ruff. I'm also assigning roles like "neck" for chain construction and writing a helper to determine left/right side naming, then building the hind leg limbs with hip and foot positions and bend arrays, making sure names stay unique per side.

Adding haunch and shoulder spheres, sweeping the leg chain with radii and color, and generating claw cones per paw aimed along the correct direction.
